scenario: Match demand
pressure_rule: Runs, balls, wickets and the normal trajectory versus the current state. Uses the notebook's frozen high-pressure cutoff.
pressure_mechanism: The innings is moving away from the required or expected scoring trajectory.

scenario: Close finish
pressure_rule: Late chase with competitive historical win odds. Uses the notebook's frozen high-pressure cutoff.
pressure_mechanism: In a late, competitive chase, a single ball can materially change the match.

scenario: Collapse or limited support
pressure_rule: Wickets and batting or bowling alternatives available. Uses the notebook's frozen high-pressure cutoff.
pressure_mechanism: Losing the striker is more costly when few credible batters remain.

scenario: Strong opposition
pressure_rule: Earlier opponent ability and form, plus current-match threat. Uses the notebook's frozen high-pressure cutoff.
pressure_mechanism: A proven opponent in form or already threatening reduces the margin for error.

scenario: Sustained attack
pressure_rule: Recent dots or wickets for the batter, recent attacks for the bowler. Uses the notebook's frozen high-pressure cutoff.
pressure_mechanism: Dot balls and wickets make it difficult to accelerate without risking another dismissal.

scenario: Personal form or knockout stakes
family: Batting through form slumps and knockouts
pressure_rule: Recent underperformance or recorded knockout stakes. Uses the notebook's frozen high-pressure cutoff.
pressure_mechanism: A measurable form slump or a recorded knockout creates a specific test of performance.

scenario: Recovering after a slow team powerplay
pressure_rule: Over 7 onward when the team ended six overs at least six runs below the mean of earlier powerplays from the same competition group and innings; at least eight earlier innings.
pressure_mechanism: The remaining overs have to make up for a team scoring shortfall.

scenario: Accelerating in overs 17 to 20
pressure_rule: Overs 17–20 with a first-innings trajectory deficit of at least 8, a chase at 9+ RPO or 25–75% earlier-state win odds, or a knockout. Any striker.
pressure_mechanism: The batting side has four overs left, with a scoring shortfall, urgent chase or close finish.

scenario: Facing the new ball after early wickets
pressure_rule: First five overs after at least one wicket has fallen; multiple wickets also qualify.
pressure_mechanism: An early wicket forces the batting side to score while protecting its remaining resources.

scenario: Switching between pace and spin
pressure_rule: Bowling changes between pace and spin since the striker last faced. At least one original pressure index must also be high.
pressure_mechanism: A striker facing an existing pressure state has to reset timing and shot selection against a different pace.

scenario: Set batter with a fresh partner
pressure_rule: Striker has faced at least 20 non-wide balls and partner fewer than six. At least one original pressure index must also be high.
pressure_mechanism: Much of the scoring burden sits with the established batter while the partner settles.

scenario: Scoring after a dot-heavy 15-ball stretch
pressure_rule: At least eight team dot balls among the striker's preceding 15 legal balls faced in the same innings. The following attempt is evaluated.
pressure_mechanism: The striker has used a substantial share of recent balls without scoring.

scenario: Established batter rebuilding after a wicket
pressure_rule: Overs 7 to 16, after at least 12 non-wide balls faced and with no more than three legal balls elapsed since a team wicket.
pressure_mechanism: The established striker needs to avoid compounding the wicket while keeping the innings moving.

scenario: Batting when the required rate is rising
pressure_rule: After the powerplay with at least 18 legal balls left, the required rate has risen by at least one run per over from 12 legal balls earlier.
pressure_mechanism: A useful scoring pace two overs ago now falls short of what the chase needs.

scenario: Facing a fresh bowler introduced after the powerplay
pressure_rule: The current bowler was introduced after 36 legal balls and has used fewer than six. At least one original pressure index must also be high.
pressure_mechanism: A batter already under pressure must adjust to a bowler with little same-match evidence to read.

scenario: Steep chase with two to four overs left
pressure_rule: 12–24 legal balls left and at least two runs needed per ball.
pressure_mechanism: Boundary scoring is needed with little time to recover a dot or dismissal.

scenario: Reachable last-over chase
pressure_rule: In the final over, 7–12 required off six balls at its start; score all subsequent attempts in that over.
pressure_mechanism: The chase is within reach, but a single dot or wicket can shift the balance.

scenario: Last over starts needing 13 or more
pressure_rule: In the final over after it started with 13+ needed off six.
pressure_mechanism: The batter is likely to need multiple boundaries against a defense expecting them.

scenario: Boundary needed off the last ball
pressure_rule: One legal ball left and 4–6 runs required.
pressure_mechanism: The innings depends on one boundary-capable opportunity.

scenario: Low runs needed with the last wicket
pressure_rule: 1–6 runs to win, up to 12 legal balls left, and exactly one wicket left.
pressure_mechanism: Even routine scoring must be attempted with no batting cover.

scenario: Large chase at the opening
pressure_rule: First 12 legal balls of a chase with a target of 190 or higher.
pressure_mechanism: The target demands an aggressive tempo from the opening overs.

scenario: Comfortable chase turning against the batting side
pressure_rule: After the powerplay with 18+ balls left, earlier-state win odds moved from at least 65% 12 balls ago to 50% or lower.
pressure_mechanism: A once-manageable chase has deteriorated and now requires a change in approach.

scenario: Ahead of the rate but running out of wickets
pressure_rule: Chase after six overs, 2–3 wickets left, and current rate at least 1 RPO above required rate.
pressure_mechanism: The scoring pace is manageable, but protecting the few remaining wickets is critical.

scenario: Steep required-rate jump in the middle overs
pressure_rule: Overs 7–16, required rate at least 10 RPO and up at least 2.5 from 12 legal balls earlier.
pressure_mechanism: The batter has to change scoring gears before the end of the innings.

scenario: First innings well below its scoring trajectory
pressure_rule: Overs 10–16 with a score at least 15 runs below the earlier same-context trajectory.
pressure_mechanism: The batting side has limited overs to recover a meaningful shortfall.

scenario: Death overs with wickets in hand but a scoring deficit
pressure_rule: First innings, overs 17–20, 6+ wickets left, and at least 12 runs behind trajectory.
pressure_mechanism: Unused batting depth creates a clear obligation to accelerate immediately.

scenario: New batter walking into a middle-overs collapse
pressure_rule: Overs 7–16, striker has faced at most 3 non-wide attempts and 2+ wickets fell in the previous 12 legal balls.
pressure_mechanism: A new batter must score while preventing recent wickets from becoming a full collapse.

scenario: Established batter loses the other established batter
pressure_rule: On strike immediately following a team wicket, with the striker having faced 16+ non-wides, the previous other batter gone, and the preceding pair having faced 24+ legal balls.
pressure_mechanism: A set batting pair was broken and the survivor now carries the scoring load.

scenario: Chasing with the tail and no deeper support
pressure_rule: Post-powerplay chase at 8+ RPO with 2–4 wickets left and at least two rated remaining batters with a top-three ability proxy at most 45/100.
pressure_mechanism: The striker must sustain the rate because a wicket exposes historically weak support.

scenario: Last batting pair still needs a meaningful chase
pressure_rule: Exactly one wicket left with at least 7 runs required and between 6 and 30 legal balls remaining.
pressure_mechanism: The pair must keep scoring without any replacement batter available.

scenario: Double strike before the innings settles
pressure_rule: First three overs with two or more team wickets already down.
pressure_mechanism: Batters must break the early wicket run while facing most of the powerplay still to come.

scenario: New finisher exposed late in a demanding chase
pressure_rule: Overs 19–20 with at least 9 RPO needed and striker has faced at most two non-wide attempts.
pressure_mechanism: There is almost no time to assess the bowler before taking scoring risks.

scenario: Team scoring squeeze after the powerplay
pressure_rule: Overs 7–16 with 10 runs or fewer scored over the previous 12 legal balls and either a first-innings deficit of 8+ or an 8+ RPO chase.
pressure_mechanism: The whole side has been stalled and the striker needs to release the pressure.

scenario: Dots at the end of a tight chase
pressure_rule: At least three preceding team dots, 6–24 legal balls left and at least 7 RPO needed.
pressure_mechanism: Recent scoreless balls have reduced the number of remaining scoring opportunities.

scenario: Two-over drought after an early wicket
pressure_rule: After at least 12 legal balls and within the first six overs, with a wicket down and at most 10 runs added over the prior 12 legal balls.
pressure_mechanism: The early wicket has been followed by a measurable scoring freeze despite powerplay opportunity.

scenario: Established batter stuck below a run a ball
pressure_rule: Striker has faced 18+ non-wides at under one run per attempt, with 9+ RPO required in a chase or an 8+ first-innings trajectory deficit.
pressure_mechanism: An established striker is using deliveries the team now needs to score from.

scenario: High-ability pace in a demanding innings
pressure_rule: Recorded pace, opponent ability at least 6.2/10 and at least one original pressure index is high.
pressure_mechanism: The batter must score against historically stronger pace while the match state already requires it.

scenario: High-ability off-spin in a demanding innings
pressure_rule: Recorded right-arm off-break, opponent ability at least 6.2/10 and at least one original pressure index is high.
pressure_mechanism: Performance against a well-rated off-spinner tests a distinct turn and scoring-angle matchup.

scenario: High-ability wrist spin in a demanding innings
pressure_rule: Recorded right-arm leg-break or left-arm wrist spin, opponent ability at least 6.2/10, and at least one original pressure index is high.
pressure_mechanism: The batter needs to score against a strong wrist spinner while reading turn and variation.

scenario: High-ability left-arm orthodox under pressure
pressure_rule: Recorded slow left-arm orthodox, opponent ability at least 6.2/10 and at least one original pressure index is high.
pressure_mechanism: The batter must adapt to this angle-and-turn matchup against a proven spinner.

scenario: High-velocity pace after an early wicket
pressure_rule: First six overs with a wicket already lost against a pace bowler averaging at least 138 km/h from 20+ prior measured balls.
pressure_mechanism: Less reaction time increases the difficulty of restoring the innings after an early wicket.

scenario: Proven bowler also dangerous in this spell
pressure_rule: Opponent has 6.2+ ability, recent form gap at least +0.15 and current-match threat at least 0.65.
pressure_mechanism: The bowler combines long-run quality, recent form and evidence of a threatening spell.

scenario: Facing a bowler who has repeatedly dismissed you
pressure_rule: At least 18 earlier head-to-head attempts, 10% or higher striker dismissal rate and an original pressure index high.
pressure_mechanism: The batter has a measured matchup risk before the delivery.

scenario: Facing a style that has suppressed your scoring
pressure_rule: At least 30 prior attempts against the recorded style, style scoring at most 80% of personal career scoring per attempt, and a chase at 8+ RPO or an 8+ first-innings deficit.
pressure_mechanism: Match demand forces scoring against a style that has historically constrained the individual.

scenario: Variable-repertoire bowler in an urgent chase
pressure_rule: After the powerplay in a chase at 9+ RPO, the current bowler has 4+ effective prior variation categories and recorded category coverage of at least 40%.
pressure_mechanism: The batter must score quickly against an opponent with multiple documented options.

scenario: Personal batting slump with a demanding chase
family: Batting through form slumps and knockouts
pressure_rule: Recorded pre-match batting form slump, at least three recent matches available, and a post-powerplay chase at 9+ RPO.
pressure_mechanism: The batter has to meet a clear scoring requirement despite recent underperformance.

scenario: Scoring burden in the knockout powerplay
family: Batting through form slumps and knockouts
pressure_rule: Recorded knockout, first six overs, with a wicket down or a chase requiring 9+ RPO.
pressure_mechanism: Early mistakes carry elimination stakes while the innings already has a material constraint.

scenario: Knockout chase at the death
family: Batting through form slumps and knockouts
pressure_rule: Recorded knockout, overs 17–20 and chase odds between 20% and 80% based on earlier states.
pressure_mechanism: The match is still live and there are too few balls left to recover from poor execution.

scenario: Knockout first-innings recovery after a collapse
family: Batting through form slumps and knockouts
pressure_rule: Recorded knockout, first innings after six overs and 2+ wickets in the prior 12 legal balls.
pressure_mechanism: The batter must rebuild a first-innings total after a collapse in an elimination match.

scenario: Knockout batter facing a proven bowler in form
family: Batting through form slumps and knockouts
pressure_rule: Recorded knockout, bowler rated at least 6.2/10 with a recent positive form gap of at least +0.15, and a high original match-demand or limited-support index.
pressure_mechanism: Elimination stakes and the adverse match state compound the difficulty of the matchup.

scenario: Match demand
pressure_rule: Runs, balls, wickets and the normal trajectory versus the current state. Uses the notebook's frozen high-pressure cutoff.
pressure_mechanism: The chasing side or first-innings batters are scoring faster than the fielding side can afford.

scenario: Close finish
pressure_rule: Late chase with competitive historical win odds. Uses the notebook's frozen high-pressure cutoff.
pressure_mechanism: In a late, competitive chase, a single ball can materially change the match.

scenario: Collapse or limited support
pressure_rule: Wickets and batting or bowling alternatives available. Uses the notebook's frozen high-pressure cutoff.
pressure_mechanism: With few credible bowling alternatives, the current bowler has more responsibility for the innings.

scenario: Strong opposition
pressure_rule: Earlier opponent ability and form, plus current-match threat. Uses the notebook's frozen high-pressure cutoff.
pressure_mechanism: A proven opponent in form or already threatening reduces the margin for error.

scenario: Sustained attack
pressure_rule: Recent dots or wickets for the batter, recent attacks for the bowler. Uses the notebook's frozen high-pressure cutoff.
pressure_mechanism: A scoring surge can remove the fielding side's remaining defensive margin.

scenario: Personal form or knockout stakes
family: Bowling through form slumps and knockouts
pressure_rule: Recent underperformance or recorded knockout stakes. Uses the notebook's frozen high-pressure cutoff.
pressure_mechanism: A measurable form slump or a recorded knockout creates a specific test of performance.

scenario: First-innings death-over containment
pressure_rule: At least 96 legal balls used and the batting side has five or more wickets left. At least one original pressure index must also be high.
pressure_mechanism: The batting side has enough wickets to attack with little concern about being bowled out.

scenario: Bowling to a settled partnership
pressure_rule: The current pair has added at least 30 runs and faced at least 24 legal balls. At least one original pressure index must also be high.
pressure_mechanism: Two batters who have already built an innings together are harder to contain or separate.

scenario: Returning for a new spell
pressure_rule: First two deliveries on return after an 18-legal-ball gap, after the powerplay. At least one original pressure index must also be high.
pressure_mechanism: The bowler has to regain rhythm immediately while the match is already under pressure.

scenario: Adjusting to a left/right switch
pressure_rule: The striker's recorded hand differs from the previous ball in the same bowler's over. At least one original pressure index must also be high.
pressure_mechanism: The bowler must adjust line and field angles mid-over while already under pressure.

scenario: Recovering after a wide or no-ball
pressure_rule: The same bowler's immediately previous attempt in the over was illegal. At least one original pressure index must also be high.
pressure_mechanism: An extra run and replacement ball reduce the bowler's room for another mistake.

scenario: Building on your own wicket in the same over
pressure_rule: A wicket was credited to this bowler one or two delivery attempts earlier in this over. At least one original pressure index must also be high.
pressure_mechanism: The bowler has a short chance to capitalize on a wicket while the innings remains under pressure.

scenario: Closing out a tight over
pressure_rule: The over has used four or five legal balls and the bowler has conceded at most six runs in it. At least one original pressure index must also be high.
pressure_mechanism: A late boundary can undo a valuable low-cost over in an already pressured spell.

scenario: Bowling the final quota over
pressure_rule: The bowler has already delivered at least 18 legal balls in this innings. At least one original pressure index must also be high.
pressure_mechanism: The bowler is using the last part of their usual four-over allocation under pressure.

scenario: Taking over after a costly wicketless over
pressure_rule: First two legal-ball positions of the over after another bowler's over cost the team at least 10 runs with no wicket. At least one original pressure index must also be high.
pressure_mechanism: The new bowler inherits an innings that has just accelerated without losing a wicket.

scenario: Bowling the 19th over
pressure_rule: Over 19 with 4+ batting wickets left and a first-innings score within 5 runs of trajectory or ahead, a chase at 7–14 RPO or 25–75% earlier-state win odds, or a knockout.
pressure_mechanism: The penultimate over leaves only six more legal balls to repair a costly spell.

scenario: Raising the required rate from a manageable chase
pressure_rule: Second innings, 12 or more legal balls remaining, and a pre-ball required rate from six to ten runs per over. At least one original pressure index must also be high.
pressure_mechanism: If the chase is manageable, beating the required pace can force the batters into higher-risk scoring.

scenario: Defending 7–12 at the start of the last over
pressure_rule: Chase opened the final over needing 7–12 off six. Evaluate each subsequent attempt in that over.
pressure_mechanism: The over is defendable, but one boundary or extra can give away the margin.

scenario: Defending six or fewer in the last over
pressure_rule: Chase opened the final over needing 1–6 off six. Evaluate subsequent attempts in that over.
pressure_mechanism: The opposition can win through routine scoring, so a wicket or sequence of dots is especially valuable.

scenario: Last legal ball with the match within reach
pressure_rule: One legal ball remains and the chasing team needs 1–6 runs.
pressure_mechanism: The bowler has one ball to manage a live result, and an extra may concede the match or another attempt.

scenario: Defending a narrow cushion in overs 17–18
pressure_rule: First two death overs and chase odds are 35–65% based on earlier match states.
pressure_mechanism: The bowler can shift a balanced chase before the designated final two overs.

scenario: Nineteenth over to a set striker in a balanced chase
pressure_rule: Over 19, striker has faced 16+ non-wides and chase win odds are 30–70% based on earlier states.
pressure_mechanism: An established batter is in position to take control of the penultimate over.

scenario: Only one wicket needed but the chase is live
pressure_rule: Exactly one batting wicket left, 7–24 legal balls remaining and 4–20 runs needed.
pressure_mechanism: Taking the wicket can finish the match, but ordinary scoring can still beat the defense.

scenario: Small target and no early defensive cushion
pressure_rule: Powerplay of a chase of 145 or fewer with required rate at most 7.5 RPO.
pressure_mechanism: A low target leaves little room to concede early boundaries before the chase becomes comfortable.

scenario: Chase shifting decisively toward the batters
pressure_rule: Post-powerplay with 18+ legal balls left, earlier-state chase odds rise from at most 50% 12 balls ago to at least 65%.
pressure_mechanism: The defense needs to reverse momentum before the batting side can cruise.

scenario: Below seven required with batting depth intact
pressure_rule: Overs 7–16, 5 to under 7 RPO required and at least six batting wickets available.
pressure_mechanism: Batters can play low-risk cricket, making sustained dots or wickets necessary to change the chase.

scenario: Required rate falls sharply over two overs
pressure_rule: After the powerplay with 18+ balls left, chase required rate fell by at least 2 RPO in 12 balls and is now 10 or less.
pressure_mechanism: The previous defensive plan has failed to hold the scoring pace.

scenario: First innings accelerating above trajectory in the middle
pressure_rule: Overs 7–16 of the first innings with a score at least 15 runs above the earlier same-context trajectory.
pressure_mechanism: A substantial scoring overshoot risks setting an unusually difficult target if left unchecked.

scenario: Explosive opposition powerplay
pressure_rule: From the start of over 5 to the end of over 6, batting team scoring at 10+ RPO with at most one wicket lost.
pressure_mechanism: Batters in control can keep attacking because the fielding side has yet to take enough wickets.

scenario: Few credible bowling alternatives left
pressure_rule: 12+ legal balls remain, at most two quota-eligible alternatives, alternate top-three ability at most 50/100, and 60%+ known-history coverage, with a high original pressure index.
pressure_mechanism: The captain has limited credible replacements, increasing the current bowler's responsibility.

scenario: First innings wicket drought while runs build
pressure_rule: From over 9 to 16, no team wicket in the previous 36 legal balls, 7+ batting wickets left and scoring at 8+ RPO.
pressure_mechanism: The fielding side needs a breakthrough before the set batters can exploit the death overs.

scenario: Protect the hard-won wicket against a strong replacement
pressure_rule: Within two legal balls after a team wicket, striker has faced at most two non-wides, is rated 6.5+/10, and a high original pressure index is active.
pressure_mechanism: The new batter is historically strong, but the defense has a brief chance before they settle.

scenario: Final quota under an urgent chase defense
pressure_rule: Bowler has used 18+ legal balls, 7–24 remain in the match, and the chase needs 7–12 RPO.
pressure_mechanism: A primary bowler has few deliveries left to protect a defendable target.

scenario: Own spell after an expensive start
pressure_rule: Bowler has completed 6–12 legal balls, has conceded at least 12 runs per six legal balls so far and taken no credited wicket.
pressure_mechanism: Prior overs have consumed the defense's margin and the bowler has to recover within the remaining quota.

scenario: Following your own conceded boundary in a live chase
pressure_rule: Immediately following a boundary on the same bowler's previous attempt in the current over, with at most 24 balls left and chase odds at 30–75%.
pressure_mechanism: The boundary made an already competitive chase more fragile. The response ball must restore control.

scenario: Taking over after a multi-over surge
pressure_rule: First two legal-ball positions of an over, after 24 legal balls; prior 12 legal balls cost 24+ runs with no wicket.
pressure_mechanism: A prolonged team scoring surge calls for immediate control from the incoming bowler.

scenario: Protecting a low-cost over against a strong finisher
pressure_rule: At least four legal balls into a death over, the bowler has conceded at most 4 in the current over, and striker is 6.5+ quality with at least 1.5 live runs per non-wide across 12+ faced.
pressure_mechanism: One late boundary can erase the bowler's progress against a batter already hitting freely.

scenario: Bowling after a runaway boundary over starts
pressure_rule: First six overs after 6+ legal balls, among the preceding six legal balls the team allowed at least three boundaries and 15+ runs.
pressure_mechanism: The matchup needs a rapid plan change under powerplay fielding constraints.

scenario: Bowling to a proven, in-form hitter already scoring freely
pressure_rule: Striker rated 6.5+/10 with recent form gap of at least +0.15, and 12+ non-wides at 1.5 or more live runs per non-wide.
pressure_mechanism: The opponent combines long-run ability, recent form and live control of the innings.

scenario: Defending late against a dangerous left-hander
pressure_rule: Recorded left-handed striker, 6.5+ ability or 12+ non-wides at 1.5+ live runs per attempt, overs 17–20, with 7–14 RPO needed.
pressure_mechanism: A capable left-hander changes the defensive angles in a chase where each delivery matters.

scenario: Defending late against a dangerous right-hander
pressure_rule: Recorded right-handed striker, 6.5+ ability or 12+ non-wides at 1.5+ live runs per attempt, overs 17–20, with 7–14 RPO needed.
pressure_mechanism: This is the complementary handedness matchup at the same defensive stakes, for measuring versatility.

scenario: Bowling to an opponent who has dominated you
pressure_rule: At least 18 earlier head-to-head attempts, striker has scored at least 1.65 runs per attempt, and an original bowler pressure index is high.
pressure_mechanism: The batter has an evidence-backed advantage against this specific bowler.

scenario: Unfavorable handedness against a quality batter
pressure_rule: At least 30 prior attempts against that batting hand, runs conceded per attempt at least 15% worse than own long-run rate, and striker rated 6.5+/10.
pressure_mechanism: A proven opponent can exploit a measured weakness in the bowler's usual matchup.

scenario: Bowling to a two-sided batting threat
pressure_rule: The pair contains both hands and each batter has 6+/10 prior ability. Current pair has faced 18+ balls and the bowler faces a high original pressure index.
pressure_mechanism: The fielding side faces two proven threats with different scoring angles and little easy matchup relief.

scenario: High-range shotmaker attacking a defendable chase
pressure_rule: Middle or death overs, chase at 7–12 RPO, striker has 4+ effective historical shot categories with 40%+ historical labels and 6.5+ ability.
pressure_mechanism: A proven batter with a wide recorded shot range can exploit a single-line defensive plan.

scenario: Bowling slump while the defense is still in play
family: Bowling through form slumps and knockouts
pressure_rule: Pre-match bowling form-slump indicator, 3+ recent matches, and a post-powerplay chase at 7–12 RPO.
pressure_mechanism: The bowler must contain a plausible chase despite persistent recent underperformance.

scenario: Knockout powerplay getting away from the defense
family: Bowling through form slumps and knockouts
pressure_rule: Recorded knockout, 12–35 legal balls used, batting rate at least 9 RPO and at most one wicket lost.
pressure_mechanism: An elimination-game powerplay is getting away without a breakthrough.

scenario: Knockout chase alive in the death overs
family: Bowling through form slumps and knockouts
pressure_rule: Recorded knockout, overs 17–20 and chase odds between 20% and 80% based on earlier states.
pressure_mechanism: Each remaining delivery can decide an elimination match.

scenario: Knockout first innings with a strong finish looming
family: Bowling through form slumps and knockouts
pressure_rule: Recorded knockout, first-innings death overs with 5+ batting wickets remaining and a score within 5 runs of trajectory or ahead.
pressure_mechanism: The batting side has enough resources to accelerate into a potentially difficult elimination-match target.

scenario: Knockout pressure against an in-form quality striker
family: Bowling through form slumps and knockouts
pressure_rule: Recorded knockout, striker rated at least 6.5/10 with a form gap of at least +0.15, and an original match-demand or close-finish index high.
pressure_mechanism: Opponent quality matters more because the match state and elimination stakes are already adverse.
